tool.name: 3Dtrees: Trajectory and Occlusion
tool.description: estimate a lidar sensor path and map occlusion
tool.command: #if $delivered_trajectory #for $i, $path in enumerate($delivered_trajectory) ln -s '$path' 'path_${i + 1}.csv' && #end for #end if python /src/run.py #for $cloud in $point_cloud '$cloud' #end for -o trajectory.csv --occlusion-copc occlusion.copc.laz --occlusion-cog occlusion.tif #if $dtm --dtm '$dtm' #end if #if $delivered_trajectory --trajectory #for $i, $path in enumerate($delivered_trajectory) 'path_${i + 1}.csv' #end for #end if --voxel $voxel --interval $interval $full --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-10}

param.name: point_cloud
param.label: Standardized LAS/LAZ point cloud
param.help: Select one dataset or a list from the same acquisition in collection order.

param.label: Digital terrain model
param.help: Select a GeoTIFF in the point cloud's CRS. Without it, ground height is estimated from the lowest returns.

param.name: delivered_trajectory
param.label: Delivered trajectories
param.help: One or more comma-separated 3Dtrees trajectories with time,x,y,z. Occlusion uses these positions when supplied.

param.label: Voxel size (m)
param.help: Occlusion voxel edge and COG height-band step. Smaller voxels need much more memory and time (0.25 m is about 8 times the grid of 0.5 m).

param.label: Use all pulses
param.help: Fit the path from every pulse (default), streamed with bounded memory. Uncheck to fit from a sample of about 40 million pulses.

tool.help:
Estimate the flight or walking path of a moving lidar scanner (ULS or MLS). Use the standardized LAS/LAZ files from one acquisition, in collection order. All files must share the same metric coordinates and GPS clock. Preserve GPS time, return metadata, scan angles, point sources and scanner channels. The tool fits a path from multi-return pulse lines or usable scan angles. Single-return data without usable scan angles needs a delivered moving path.
An optional digital terrain model (e.g. the 3Dtrees Raster DTM) sets the ground. It may have no CRS; nodata and uncovered cells use the lowest-hit ground estimate. A delivered path may be in any EPSG CRS and is converted to the point cloud's CRS; "local" in its header or in the outputs means the point cloud's own coordinates. One or more delivered paths may be given; each part of the cloud uses the path that covers its time and fits best. Both occlusion outputs use 0.5 m voxels by default.
**Outputs**
- **Trajectory CSV** with estimated positions, their GPS times and quality metadata. - **Occlusion COPC** with voxel classes, traversal counts and height above ground. - **Occlusion COG** with the occluded fraction by height band and an unobserved-column band.
With a delivered path, the tool uses it for occlusion and still tries to estimate the trajectory outputs. Those outputs can be empty if fitting fails. If occlusion cannot run (for example on a COPC instead of the standardized LAS/LAZ, or a delivered path that covers too little of the flight), the job fails with the reason.
Details, exit codes and resources: https://github.com/3dTrees-earth/3dtrees_trajectory
